findings.title: T13's "reuse 320's existing result-discovery surface" does not exist; the sanctioned fallback cannot satisfy the non-empty-offers guarantee
findings.description: The design's success criterion "a graduated config with unsampled results yields a non-empty offer set (asserted by test)" is the load-bearing commitment, but the premise of T13's primary branch is factually false: the only review-directory enumeration in the codebase is `resolve_target`, which globs `{index}-review.*` for a caller-supplied index — there is no surface that enumerates *all* persisted judge results (verified: no `list_reviews`/`discover*` for the reviews dir anywhere in `src/squadron`; `_REVIEWS_DIR` is used only by `review/persistence.py:17,236,279`). The fallback branch — "scope to the store-recorded samples only" — is incoherent for the guarantee: "unsampled" is defined as *no `SampleVerdict.result_ref` points at it*, so store records alone can never contain an unsampled result. The same missing enumeration also breaks T13/T14's lapsed-graduation detection (needs current judge results to compare identity against) and the pruned-file case. As written, a junior AI either fails the guarantee test or invents the file-walk the task forbids. Remedy: replace "reuse 320's existing surface" with an explicit step in T13 that adds a discovery helper (e.g. scan `<cwd>/project-documents/user/reviews` + `derive_judge_config_id` per file, reusing the frontmatter reader — capture.py already owns `_REVIEWS_SUBDIR`), and define the lapse-vs-exhausted signal in the return type rather than leaving it "whatever signal T13 produces."

findings.title: Malformed-`judge:`-block failure row is claimed covered by T8 but no task implements or tests it
findings.description: The design's Failure Modes table row "threshold read | malformed `judge:` block (non-numeric floor) | fall back to `resolve_thresholds`' documented merge | WARNING naming the template | malformed judge block → flagged, not silently defaulted" has an explicit Test column, and the task's Coverage Check asserts it is "exercised in T8". T7's steps and success line only cover the *unregistered template* case, and T8 has no malformed-judge bullet. This matters: `resolve_thresholds` does `float(pass_floor)` on the template value, so a non-numeric floor raises `ValueError`/`TypeError` — it does not "fall back" to the module constant for a *present-but-malformed* key. Because T9 calls `read_current_thresholds` per cell, one malformed template would crash the whole read-only `recommend` command. Add a T7 bullet (catch the coercion failure per cell, return `None` or flag the target, WARNING naming the template) and a corresponding T8 test.

findings.title: The runtime-drawn-model half of `model_dimension_note` is unassigned and unasserted
findings.description: Functional requirement 4 bundles two assertions: the model+threshold pairing on every recommendation *and* "the runtime-drawn-model limitation is stated where the recommendation is produced." The design's mismatch section is explicit: "Where a step draws its model at runtime (a 180 pool), the note states that the threshold cannot track the drawn model — the recommendation does not apply to that step." T9's note-text bullet covers only the first clause; the Context Summary's line 19 mentions the (template,model)↔(template,step) mismatch but not the pool case; and neither T10 nor T16 asserts the pool clause. A junior AI implementing the given steps will ship a note that silently omits it, and no test catches it. Add the clause to T9's bullet and one T16/T10 assertion string to check for.

findings.title: Graduate orchestration is placed in the CLI shell, violating the slice's own thin-shell/parity rule; and the CLI has no defined way to resolve the `JudgeConfigId` hash
findings.description: T15 states "thin shells, all logic in `calibration.py`/`graduation.py`", yet its `graduate` bullet contains the entire decision procedure: re-derive the report, filter the pairing, refuse non-`GRADUATE`, construct `GraduatedConfig`, and perform the idempotent in-place update. None of T9–T13 defines a core function for this, so the logic lands in Typer code (breaking the parity commitment the design's Special Considerations demand) or gets invented untested. Two concrete gaps this creates: (1) the flags are `--template/--model/--level` with no hash — when multiple cells share `(template, model, level)` with different `template_content_hash` values (exactly the segregation 321 produces for unversioned records), the task never says which cell's identity becomes the graduation; (2) if the implementer reaches for the convenience of 320's `_judge_config_matches` (store.py:73-86) to find the existing record, its "compare hash only when the filter specifies one" wildcard semantics would silently re-open the F002 version-blending bug. Fix: add a `graduate_pairing(store, agreement, template, model, level, ...) -> GraduatedOutcome` core task between T13 and T15, specify that ambiguity resolves by refusing (or requiring the hash-bearing `GRADUATE` cell), and tell T11 not to reuse `_judge_config_matches` for version-scoped matching.

findings.title: T11's "extract a shared helper" forces a refactor of 320's `list_samples`, in tension with "the capture path (320) is unchanged"
findings.description: No shared tolerant-scan helper exists today — the `(OSError, ValueError, SchemaVersionError)` skip loop is inline in `list_samples`. The technical requirement permits adding the `graduated_config` discriminator/field but says 320 is otherwise unchanged. Suggest scoping T11's helper as an *added* private method used only by `list_graduations` (and, if touched, `list_samples` delegating with no behavior change), so 320/321 store tests remain untouched and the T17 gate is trivial.

findings.title: T2's target file splits coverage of the same hash the existing tests already cover elsewhere
findings.description: The existing `derive_judge_config_id` / `template_content_hash` assertions live in `test_result_ref.py` (`TestJudgeConfigId`), while `test_identity.py` covers project-id derivation. T2's "Extend `tests/metrology/test_identity.py` (or add … check first)" will most naturally land the `derive_judge_config_id` end-to-end bullet away from its existing sibling tests. Naming `test_result_ref.py#TestJudgeConfigId` as the home for the third bullet avoids split coverage; also note those tests must register `ReviewTemplate`s (the registry is only populated by `load_all_templates()` on CLI/pipeline paths, per review/templates/\_\_init\_\_.py).

findings.title: One `**Commit:**` marker after every task (17), including 8 implementation tasks whose tests land next
findings.description: Markers are plain (non-checkbox) lines with semantic messages — correct form — and CLAUDE.md mandates "at least once per task," so this is convention-compliant and matches the 320/321 precedent; recorded only as informational. If the pair-level reading is preferred, T1+T2 and T15+T16 are the candidates to share a single marker, since their success states only exist once both land.
